title: Requirements and output contracts
summary: Quantity can be measured by a party’s good-faith requirements or output rather than a fixed number.
notes: Structural Polymer explains why variable or temporarily zero requirements need not make an agreement illusory. The source inquiry includes whether demand is genuine, the role of a price-matching clause, and the good-faith constraints associated with UCC § 2-306. The breadcrumb-output problem asks whether shutting production after losses is consistent with the bargain. The full assigned statutory text remains a separate source item where the excerpt only discusses it.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 107–113. Open assigned page 107.
